For statistical analysis, you can use Lee's L statistic for bivariate spatial correlation analysis, or another appropriate method of your choosing. You are testing whether Gas in one place relates to Crime in NEIGHBORING places.

Determine whether the two variables show a significant bivariate spatial relationship. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. Implement this directly using only pandas and numpy. import pandas as pd
```python
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2021_gas_crime.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Find the borough with NaN Crime
nan_borough = df.loc[df['Crime_value'].isna(), 'borough'].values[0]
print('Borough with NaN Crime:', nan_borough)

# Drop the borough with missing Crime
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=['Crime_value']).copy()
boroughs = sorted(df_clean['borough'].unique())
n = len(boroughs)
print('Remaining boroughs:', n)
print(boroughs)

borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Build symmetric adjacency set excluding the dropped borough
edge_set = set()
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    u = row['borough']
    v = row['neighbor']
    if u == nan_borough or v == nan_borough:
        continue
    if u != v:
        edge_set.add((u, v))
        edge_set.add((v, u))

# Build row-standardized W matrix
W = np.zeros((n, n))
for i, b in enumerate(boroughs):
    neighbors = [v for v in boroughs if v != b and (b, v) in edge_set]
    d = len(neighbors)
    if d > 0:
        for v in neighbors:
            j = borough_to_idx[v]
            W[i, j] = 1.0 / d
    else:
        print(f'Warning: {b} has no neighbors after dropping {nan_borough}')

print('W row sums:', W.sum(axis=1))

# Get Gas and Crime aligned to borough order
gas = df_clean.set_index('borough').loc[boroughs, 'Gas_value'].values
crime = df_clean.set_index('borough').loc[boroughs, 'Crime_value'].values

# Standardize to mean 0, variance 1 (population)
z_gas = (gas - gas.mean()) / gas.std(ddof=0)
z_crime = (crime - crime.mean()) / crime.std(ddof=0)

print('z_gas mean, std:', z_gas.mean(), z_gas.std(ddof=0))
print('z_crime mean, std:', z_crime.mean(), z_crime.std(ddof=0))

# Lee's L statistic
L_obs = (z_gas @ (W @ z_crime)) / n
print('Observed Lee L:', L_obs)

# Permutation test with 1000 shuffles
np.random.seed(42)
n_perm = 1000
L_perm = np.zeros(n_perm)

for i in range(n_perm):
    z_gas_perm = np.random.permutation(z_gas)
    L_perm[i] = (z_gas_perm @ (W @ z_crime)) / n

# Two-tailed p-value
p_value = np.mean(np.abs(L_perm) >= np.abs(L_obs))
print('Permutation p-value:', p_value)
print('Null mean:', L_perm.mean())
print('Null std:', L_perm.std())
print('Min null:', L_perm.min())
print('Max null:', L_perm.max())
```
